notes: Growth privacy-filter switch. Adds a deployment-level switch GROWTH_PRIVACY_FILTER whose default (strict) reproduces the previous behavior exactly. With off, the PII pattern rejection is disabled: GSC query rows and GA4 dimension rows are no longer dropped when they look like an email address, a phone / 10+ digit run, a token/secret assignment, a control character or over-long text, and the day is no longer marked privacy_filtered_rows (that mark made the 56-day window one day short and pushed candidate generation out by weeks — the concrete case was 2026-09-29, where GSC returned 2 query rows and the platform's own filter removed 1). URL normalization and tracking-parameter handling are deliberately NOT affected: they are page-identity rules, and disabling them would split one page into several identities and fragment historical statistics; operator-entered labels/notes keep their isSafeGrowthQuery validation because that is input validation, not site-visitor data. The switch is read from process.env rather than runtimeEnvironment() because collection and ingest run inside withRuntimeEnvironment(organization env), a fresh object that only holds organization keys — reading the latter would silently fall back to strict, i.e. the opposite of the deployment setting. bootstrap/compose.yml passes GROWTH_PRIVACY_FILTER through to api/worker/dispatcher (default strict) and documents that turning it off means the platform starts processing raw search terms that may contain personal data, so the /privacy and /google-data wording must match the deployment's actual behaviour. No SQL migration and no schema change. Rollback to v0.2.18 is compatible; because the switch defaults to strict, a rollback simply re-enables filtering. Rows already dropped are not recoverable, and a snapshot already marked privacy_filtered_rows keeps its mark until that day is re-collected (a re-collection with the switch off produces a clean snapshot); history is never rewritten.
